source.original_text: Canonical background expansion of the source uniform-sphere sentence: for every positive finite dimension \(n\) and every coordinate \(j\), let \(E=\mathbb R^n\), \(S=\{u:\|u\|_2=1\}\), and \(\mu\) be the actual normalized Haar probability on full \(O(n)\). Let \(\tau\) be the actual Euclidean-volume cone surface measure, \(\tau(B)=n\,\mathrm{vol}\{ru:0<r<1,u\in B\}\), and let \(\sigma=\tau(S)^{-1}\iota_*\tau\) on E. Then the actual pushforward \((O\mapsto Oe_j)_*\mu\) equals \(\sigma\). This explicitly generalizes the source use at its first coordinate with \(n\ge3\); it asserts no conditional residual law, independence, Poisson value, or lower bound.

blind_reconstruction.text:
For every natural number n and every coordinate index j in Fin n = {0,...,n-1}, consider the real Euclidean space R^n with its genuine l2 norm, its Borel structure, and its Euclidean volume measure. Put S = {u in R^n : ||u||_2 = 1}. Let tau be volume.toSphere, a measure on the sphere subtype S, with the cone-derived normalization: for a Borel subset B of S, tau(B) = n times volume({t*u : 0 < t < 1, u in B}). Let i:S -> R^n be inclusion and define the ambient measure sigma = (tau(S))^(-1) times i_*tau. Here the mass and its reciprocal, and scalar multiplication of measures, are in the extended nonnegative reals.

Let H be Haar probability on the entire real orthogonal group O(n), including matrices of both determinant signs, with the inherited matrix Borel structure. Define c_j:O(n) -> R^n by c_j(O) = (O_{0j},...,O_{n-1,j}); these coordinates are assembled as an l2 Euclidean vector. The assertion is the equality of ambient measures (c_j)_*H = sigma. In particular, for every Borel subset A of R^n, H({O : c_j(O) in A}) = (tau(S))^(-1) tau({u in S : i(u) in A}), with the right-hand side interpreted as extended nonnegative real measure scaling.

The quantifiers have no hypotheses other than n being natural and j being an element of Fin n. Thus an actual index requires n >= 1; the n = 0 case is vacuous because Fin 0 is empty. The equality holds for each chosen column, with the same normalized cone-derived sphere measure. This is a single-column distribution statement; it does not assert independence or a joint distribution of different columns, and it is not an assertion for Haar measure restricted to the special orthogonal group. No asymptotic parameter, estimate, auxiliary constant, or regularity hypothesis occurs.

import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Constructions.HaarToSphere
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.Haar.InnerProductSpace
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Projection.Reflection
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.Prod
open Matrix MeasureTheory
open AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.OrthogonalHaar
namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.SphereHaar
set_option autoImplicit false
/-!
Canonical actual full-orthogonal Haar column law on Euclidean space.
The surface measure is derived from actual Euclidean volume by the cone
construction and finite nonzero normalization. No invariant-law identity,
conditional law or Poisson evaluation is assumed.
-/
open Set Metric
open scoped Pointwise ENNReal
theorem column_map_eq_normalized_surface {n : ℕ} (j : Fin n) :
    let τ : Measure (Metric.sphere (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) 1) :=
      (volume : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))).toSphere
    let σ : Measure (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) :=
      (τ Set.univ)⁻¹ • τ.map (fun y => y.val)
    (orthogonalHaar n).map
      (fun O : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ => WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) i j)) = σ := by
  classical
  let : NeZero n := ⟨by have := j.isLt; omega⟩
  let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)
  let G := Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ
  let S := Metric.sphere (0 : E) 1
  let τ : Measure S := (volume : Measure E).toSphere
  let σ : Measure E := (τ univ)⁻¹ • τ.map Subtype.val
  let c : G → E := fun O => WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) i j)
  let T : G → E →L[ℝ] E := fun O =>
    Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℝ) (n := Fin n) (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ)
  let μ := orthogonalHaar n
  let ν : Measure E := μ.map c
  have hc : Continuous c :=
    (PiLp.continuous_toLp 2 (fun _ : Fin n => ℝ)).comp
      (continuous_pi (fun i => continuous_subtype_val.matrix_elem i j))
  let := (orthogonalHaar_spec n).1
  let : NeZero τ := ⟨Measure.toSphere_ne_zero volume⟩
  let ρ : Measure S := (τ univ)⁻¹ • τ
  have hρ : IsProbabilityMeasure ρ := inferInstance
  have hσ : σ = ρ.map Subtype.val := by rw [Measure.map_smul]
  let := hρ
  have hσprob : IsProbabilityMeasure σ := by
    rw [hσ]
    exact Measure.isProbabilityMeasure_map measurable_subtype_coe.aemeasurable
  let := hσprob
  have hσsphere : ∀ᵐ y ∂σ, ‖y‖ = 1 := by
    rw [hσ]
    apply (ae_map_iff measurable_subtype_coe.aemeasurable
      (isClosed_eq continuous_norm continuous_const).measurableSet).2
    exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall (fun y => mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm.mp y.property)
  have hσiso (Q : E ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] E) : σ.map Q = σ := by
    classical
    let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)
    let S := Metric.sphere (0 : E) 1
    let τ : Measure S := (volume : Measure E).toSphere
    let q : S → S := fun y => ⟨Q y, by
      change Q (y : E) ∈ Metric.sphere (0 : E) 1
      rw [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm, Q.norm_map]
      exact mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm.mp y.property⟩
    have hq : Measurable q := (Q.continuous.comp continuous_subtype_val).subtype_mk _ |>.measurable
    have hτ : τ.map q = τ := by
      ext t ht
      rw [Measure.map_apply hq ht]
      change (volume : Measure E).toSphere (q ⁻¹' t) = (volume : Measure E).toSphere t
      rw [Measure.toSphere_apply' _ (ht.preimage hq), Measure.toSphere_apply' _ ht]
      congr 1
      have hc : Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 • (Subtype.val '' (q ⁻¹' t)) =
          Q ⁻¹' (Ioo (0 : ℝ) 1 • (Subtype.val '' t)) := by
        ext x
        constructor
        · rintro ⟨a, ha, z, ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
          exact ⟨a, ha, Q y, ⟨q y, hy, rfl⟩, (Q.map_smul a y).symm⟩
        · rintro ⟨a, ha, z, ⟨y, hy, rfl⟩, hxy⟩
          let w : S := ⟨Q.symm y, by
            change Q.symm (y : E) ∈ Metric.sphere (0 : E) 1
            rw [mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm, Q.symm.norm_map]
            exact mem_sphere_zero_iff_norm.mp y.property⟩
          have hw : q w = y := by apply Subtype.ext; exact Q.apply_symm_apply y
          refine ⟨a, ha, Q.symm y, ⟨w, ?_, rfl⟩, ?_⟩
          · change q w ∈ t
            rw [hw]
            exact hy
          · apply Q.injective
            simpa using hxy
      rw [hc]
      exact Q.measurePreserving.measure_preimage_emb Q.toHomeomorph.measurableEmbedding _
    change ((τ univ)⁻¹ • τ.map Subtype.val).map Q = (τ univ)⁻¹ • τ.map Subtype.val
    rw [Measure.map_smul, Measure.map_map Q.continuous.measurable measurable_subtype_coe]
    have he : (Q : E → E) ∘ Subtype.val = Subtype.val ∘ q := rfl
    rw [he, ← Measure.map_map measurable_subtype_coe hq, hτ]
  have hσinv (O : G) : σ.map (T O) = σ := by
    let u : unitary (E →L[ℝ] E) :=
      ⟨T O, Unitary.map_mem (Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℝ) (n := Fin n)) O.property⟩
    exact hσiso (Unitary.linearIsometryEquiv u)
  have horbit : ∀ y : E, ‖y‖ = 1 → μ.map (fun O : G => T O y) = ν := by
    classical
    let E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)
    let G := Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ
    let j0 : Fin n := j
    let c : G → E := fun O => WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) i j0)
    let T : G → E →L[ℝ] E := fun O =>
      Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℝ) (n := Fin n) (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ)
    let e0 : E := PiLp.single 2 j0 (1 : ℝ)
    have hc : Continuous c :=
      (PiLp.continuous_toLp 2 (fun _ : Fin n => ℝ)).comp
        (continuous_pi (fun i => continuous_subtype_val.matrix_elem i j0))
    have he (O : G) : T O e0 = c O := by
      apply (WithLp.equiv 2 (Fin n → ℝ)).injective
      change (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *ᵥ Pi.single j0 1 = fun i =>
        (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) i j0
      rw [Matrix.mulVec_single_one]
      rfl
    have hr (Q : G) : (orthogonalHaar n).map (fun O => O * Q) = orthogonalHaar n := by
      let := (orthogonalHaar_spec n).1
      let := (orthogonalHaar_spec n).2.1
      exact (orthogonalHaar_spec n).2.2 _
        (Measure.isProbabilityMeasure_map (measurable_mul_const Q).aemeasurable)
        (Measure.isHaarMeasure_map_mul_right (orthogonalHaar n) Q)
    change ∀ y : E, ‖y‖ = 1 → (orthogonalHaar n).map (fun O : G => T O y) = (orthogonalHaar n).map c
    intro y hy
    let w : E ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] E := (ℝ ∙ (e0 - y))ᗮ.reflection
    let b := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ
    let Q : G := ⟨w.toMatrix b.toBasis b.toBasis, w.toMatrix_mem_unitaryGroup b b⟩
    have hw : w e0 = y := Submodule.reflection_sub (by
      change ‖(PiLp.single 2 j0 (1 : ℝ) : E)‖ = ‖y‖
      rw [PiLp.norm_single]
      simpa using hy.symm)
    have hQ : T Q e0 = y := by
      apply (WithLp.equiv 2 (Fin n → ℝ)).injective
      have hm := LinearMap.toMatrix_mulVec_repr b.toBasis b.toBasis w.toLinearEquiv.toLinearMap e0
      change (Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) *ᵥ WithLp.ofLp e0 = WithLp.ofLp (w e0) at hm
      exact hm.trans (congrArg WithLp.ofLp hw)
    have hm (O : G) : T O y = c (O * Q) := by
      rw [← hQ, ← he]
      change (Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℝ) (n := Fin n) (O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ))
        ((Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℝ) (n := Fin n) (Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ)) e0) =
        (Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (𝕜 := ℝ) (n := Fin n)
          ((O : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) * (Q : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ))) e0
      rw [map_mul]
      rfl
    change (orthogonalHaar n).map (fun O => T O y) = (orthogonalHaar n).map c
    calc
      _ = (orthogonalHaar n).map (c ∘ fun O => O * Q) := by congr 1; funext O; exact hm O
      _ = ((orthogonalHaar n).map (fun O => O * Q)).map c :=
        (Measure.map_map hc.measurable (measurable_mul_const Q)).symm
      _ = _ := by rw [hr]
  have hact : Continuous (fun p : G × E => T p.1 p.2) := by
    change Continuous (fun p : G × E => WithLp.toLp 2
      (fun i => ∑ k : Fin n, (p.1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) i k * WithLp.ofLp p.2 k))
    apply (PiLp.continuous_toLp 2 (fun _ : Fin n => ℝ)).comp
    apply continuous_pi
    intro i
    apply continuous_finsetSum
    intro k _
    exact ((continuous_subtype_val.comp continuous_fst).matrix_elem i k).mul
      ((continuous_apply k).comp
        ((PiLp.continuous_ofLp 2 (fun _ : Fin n => ℝ)).comp continuous_snd))
  change ν = σ
  ext t ht
  let g : E → ℝ≥0∞ := t.indicator (fun _ => 1)
  have hg : Measurable g := measurable_const.indicator ht
  have hgint (η : Measure E) : (∫⁻ x, g x ∂η) = η t := by
    simp [g, lintegral_indicator ht]
  have hleft (O : G) : (∫⁻ y, g (T O y) ∂σ) = σ t := by
    rw [← lintegral_map hg (T O).continuous.measurable, hσinv, hgint]
  have hright : ∀ᵐ y ∂σ, (∫⁻ O : G, g (T O y) ∂μ) = ν t := by
    filter_upwards [hσsphere] with y hy
    have hymeas : Measurable (fun O : G => T O y) :=
      (hact.comp (continuous_id.prodMk (continuous_const (y := y)))).measurable
    rw [← lintegral_map hg hymeas, horbit y hy, hgint]
  calc
    ν t = ∫⁻ y : E, ∫⁻ O : G, g (T O y) ∂μ ∂σ := by
      rw [lintegral_congr_ae hright]
      simp
    _ = ∫⁻ O : G, ∫⁻ y : E, g (T O y) ∂σ ∂μ :=
      (lintegral_lintegral_swap (μ := μ) (ν := σ)
        (f := fun O : G => fun y : E => g (T O y))
        (hg.comp hact.measurable).aemeasurable).symm
    _ = σ t := by
      simp_rw [hleft]
      rw [lintegral_const, (orthogonalHaar_spec n).1.measure_univ, mul_one]

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.SphereHaar

notation.text: The actual cone-derived surface measure on the sphere subtype, normalized and included in the ambient Euclidean space. The inverse scalar is an extended nonnegative real.
Index j in Fin n is zero-based in Lean; e_j is the corresponding actual Euclidean basis vector.

steps.title: Normalize the actual surface measure
steps.text: The cone construction has finite nonzero total mass in positive dimension. Normalize that measure on the sphere, then push it into Euclidean space. The result is a probability supported on the unit sphere.
steps.lean: Measure.toSphere_ne_zero and the canonical IsFiniteMeasure instance justify inverse scaling via isProbabilityMeasureSMul. hσ is the literal map_smul equality; hσprob and hσsphere use probability pushforward and ae_map_iff.

steps.title: Use volume preservation on cones
steps.text: Every linear isometry preserves Euclidean volume and commutes with positive radial scaling. Its action therefore preserves the cone-derived surface measure and its normalized ambient pushforward, including orientation-reversing maps.
steps.lean: hσiso constructs the actual sphere subtype map q. hτ applies Measure.toSphere_apply' and proves exact cone preimage equality hc; LinearIsometryEquiv.measurePreserving.measure_preimage_emb supplies actual volume preservation even for arbitrary cone sets. Measure.map_map/map_smul transport the result. hσinv uses Unitary.map_mem and Unitary.linearIsometryEquiv on Matrix.toEuclideanCLM.

steps.title: Identify every unit-vector orbit law
steps.text: For any unit vector y, a reflection sends e_j to y. Its matrix Q belongs to full O(n). Right multiplication by Q preserves the actual normalized Haar law, so O y and the j-th Haar column have the same law. No measurable choice of Q as a function of y is required.
steps.lean: horbit constructs one fixed reflection for each point using Submodule.reflection_sub, its orthonormal-basis matrix and LinearMap.toMatrix_mulVec_repr. hr derives right invariance from the identical orthogonalHaar_spec uniqueness and Measure.isHaarMeasure_map_mul_right. No clone or promotion of KernelAxis private helpers is used.

steps.title: Compare Borel events by Haar averaging
steps.text: For a Borel event B, integrate its indicator after the orthogonal action. Integrating in the sphere variable first gives sigma(B) by invariance; integrating in the Haar variable first gives nu_j(B) on the actual sphere support. The joint action is continuous, so Tonelli permits exchanging these nonnegative integrals.
steps.lean: hact proves joint Euclidean continuity from finite matrix-coordinate sums and PiLp topology. hg is the Borel indicator into ENNReal. hleft uses actual sigma invariance; hright uses horbit on hσsphere. lintegral_lintegral_swap applies with both actual probability measures; no signed Fubini or unstated L1 premise is needed.

steps.title: Conclude equality of actual measures
steps.text: The two probabilities agree on every Borel event, hence are the same ambient measure. The selected Gaussian consumer can now use the canonical surface law; conditional residual sphere laws and Poisson values remain separate.
steps.lean: Measure.ext closes the actual measure equality after Tonelli and both total masses one. The selected SurfaceLaw adapter calls this exact shared declaration, and the focused test compares two distinct actual column marginals through the same canonical node.
